title: One rule decides whether a declared path covers a file
description: F581 (priority: 68 false commit-scope breaches on a real user's first sign-off), F579, F592. Today one files entry has several meanings: commit-scope matches exact paths after stripping the slash; the plan gate and two guard hooks treat an entry as a directory only with a trailing slash (the guards through drifted inline copies); remind-tdd matches exactly; staging and run-test-gate are separator-bounded; the red-first fix tree copies files only. Settled with the user 2026-10-09: one separator-bounded predicate, hosted at L1 in scripts/manifest/_task_outputs.py, reached by hooks through _config._load_scripts_module. The next version ships only once every open bug is fixed (user, 2026-10-09).
desiredOutcome: Every reader of a task's files answers coverage through one shared predicate (an entry covers itself and everything under entry/, with or without a trailing slash), and the records a task's close and sign-off write are true: no false commit-scope breach or could-not-prove from a declared directory or a forwarded --selftest, no done task with its work uncommitted, findings carry their fix or disposition, and no committed record carries a machine path.

tasks.title: covers(): one coverage predicate, and the plan gate and every hook ask it
tasks.description: Add covers(entry, path) to _task_outputs.py (L1): strip a :line-range suffix, normalise backslashes, e = entry.rstrip('/'); True when path == e or path starts with e + '/'. A falsy entry covers nothing. output_covers reuses it for its directory arm. hooks/_config.covering_key answers through it (loaded via _load_scripts_module) and keeps its shape: the key that covers, or None, and None when the rule cannot be loaded (uncovered, the loud direction). guard-bash-writes.py and guard-secrets-read.py delete their inline copies and call covering_key; remind-tdd.py uses covering_key instead of an exact .get(rel). Cases: an entry with and without the slash covers a file under it; a sibling with a shared prefix (src vs src-old/a) is not covered; an exact file entry still covers only itself; the guards and the nudge agree with the plan gate on a slash-less directory. State the rule once in the schema's files description and manifest-conventions.md. Red-first each case against the old matcher.

tasks.title: done refuses while the task's work sits uncommitted, and start refuses a task with no files
tasks.description: F592, twice on the testbed: a task with no declared files closed done while its work sat uncommitted, because commit-task-work stages only declared files. done --commit (_locked_done) checks nothing about the tree; only the --no-change path asks git porcelain, through _no_change_moves, which this should reuse rather than re-spell. Add: done refuses when the working tree holds changes (git status, untracked included, ignoring the journal and evidence directories and the manifest files) that are covered by the task's files but absent from --commit, or, when the task declares no files, any change no other in_progress task covers; the refusal names the paths and offers /audit:task scope to widen. start refuses a task whose files is empty unless it is --no-change shaped; say what to declare. Cases for: clean tree closes; a covered leftover refuses; an empty-files task with leftovers refuses; another in-progress task's files are not blamed. Update commands/task.md and README.md's done paragraph.

tasks.title: closing a fix task records the fix on its findings, and sign-off records every open finding's disposition
tasks.description: F601 (testbed, P1 sign-off): the drive's fix path (add --fixes, then the task's own done) never writes commit/status onto the finding; only resolve-finding does, and review_tally counts only findings with both fixTask and commit. P1's signed-off manifest says 0 fixed over six fixed findings, and a med finding left open on the owner's decision vanished with status null. Fix: done on a task whose fixes names findings writes commit and status fixed onto each, in the same write as the close (no second verb to remember); signoff over open findings records each one's disposition (accepted-open with the human's reason, or carried as a bug or parked task) and refuses a null status reaching a done phase. Update phase-signoff.md and the README's signoff row.

tasks.title: every string the plugin writes into a committed plan, journal or evidence row is scrubbed of machine paths at the write
tasks.description: F604, the second recurrence of F538 (committed shards carrying machine paths): the red helper's sandbox description put the absolute project root and a home-shorthand npmrc path into P122's committed shard twice (P122.1 and P122.2 records), and check-committed-pii failed the next task gates until the orchestrator redacted them by hand. The writer already refuses a machine path in a --description (audit-task's prose-flag check through _journal_io.machine_path_shape), but text the plugin composes itself bypasses that door. Invariant: the save boundary (_manifest_io's shard/index writer, the journal append, the evidence append) passes every string value through _journal_io's existing redaction (redacted_free_text / redacted_text with the project root) so no caller can bypass it; check-committed-pii stays the backstop. Keep the layers legal (_deps.LAYERS); no new detector - reuse the ones the tool already imports. Red-first: the case in tests.add, plus a journal and an evidence row with the same shape. Layer decision (2026-10-09): _manifest_io and _journal_io are both L1 and may not import each other, so the detectors and redaction (machine_path_shape, redacted_free_text and their patterns) move into a new L0 module scripts/_machine_paths.py that both import; _journal_io keeps re-exporting the names the tool and other callers use. Use the existing tokens (repo-relative, <outside-repo>); do not invent <project>/<home>. Measured cost: about 50 ms to scrub the largest shard (P118, ~199 KB) against ~1 ms to save it - add a cheap pre-reject (a string with none of the characters a machine path needs is skipped) and re-measure twice with a gap.
